newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France strike cuts into short-haul flights.
newsitem.headline: Air France strike cuts into short-haul flights.

text.p: Air France said it was cancelling half of its short-haul services and a quarter of medium-haul trips on Wednesday, the second day of a four-day pilots' strike.
The stoppage, which began five days before parliamentary elections, is a resumption of a walkout threatened last month.
Talks with management broke down over plans to pay new pilots between nine and 30 percent less than current crews, depending on experience.
Five of six pilots unions which launched the strike remained off the job. One of the smaller unions, the SPAC, settled its differences with the airline on Tuesday.

The airline planned to implement the new pay scale in a merger with its short-haul arm Air Inter Europe, intended to make them more competitive as European airlines are opened up to cross-border competition.
Air France Chairman Christian Blanc has urged pilots to ignore the strike, saying it would wipe out the entire projected profit for 1997/98 and endanger the future of the state-owned airline.
But unions accuse him of over-dramatising.

Air France wants to hire 450 experienced pilots in the next 18 months and would pay them gross starting salaries of 320,000 francs ($56,400) a year, nine percent less than pilots with similar experience now on staff.

In a separate protest, dairy farmers in Normandy maintained roadblocks at two distribution firms, turning back delivery trucks and blocking deliveries to hypermarkets in the area, in a continuing protest over falling wholesale milk prices.
The protest had begun on Tuesday when 10,000 dairy farmers blocked access to distribution centres across France, accusing them of gradually bringing down prices.
Agriculture Minister Philippe Vasseur was holding talks in Paris on Wednesday with milk producers, processors and distributors in an effort to resolve the dispute.
